note: Candidates reviewed for this update but not admitted, with the reason and the evidence that would reopen each.

entries.candidate: CRA (České Radiokomunikace) DC Lužice, Lužice u Hodonína, South Moravia - existing operations including CRA's NVIDIA GPU-as-a-service infrastructure
entries.reason: CRA's press release of 26 October 2026 (local cra-cra-v-cesku-suverenni-ai-infrastrukturu-na-platforme-nvidia.html and cra-press-release-261026-nvidia.pdf) says CRA today operates more than twenty NVIDIA HGX/DGX B300 systems, that the NVIDIA infrastructure is so far concentrated in the Lužice data centre in South Moravia, whose capacity is practically always sold out, and that customers train and run models on it: a dated, facility-specific operating statement. CRA's DC Lužice page (cra-dc-luzice.html; www.dcluzice.cz redirects to it) describes a Tier III (design) data centre for up to 82 racks in Lužice near Hodonín, inside a closed and guarded area, owned by CRA's wholly owned subsidiary Datové centrum Lužice s.r.o. No accessible source gives the facility's address, parcel or coordinates: the page, the product leaflet (schematic location map only) and four tariff/terms PDFs give only the Prague registered offices; CRA's data-centre map page uses schematic percentage pin positions; the ARES trade-licence record of the subsidiary lists only Prague establishments; the Lužice municipal host did not respond; the commercial-register UI (or.justice.cz /ias/) is robots-disallowed; OSM object/API paths, Nominatim and Overpass are not used. A municipality-level point is not admissible.
entries.reopen_condition: An official or operator record giving the DC Lužice building address, cadastral parcel or coordinates (for example a building or occupancy permit, a RÚIAN address published by CRA or the municipality, or a CRA facility page with an address), read while the 26 October 2026 observation is within the window (about 19 January 2027 for an 85-day window); then admit as operational on 26 October 2026 with that locator.

The October 2026 CMO blog post about the Nordic Business Forum mentions launching a new 10 MW AI-ready data centre and six data centres, but its capture carries no publication date and no site-specific dated observation. Identity is also blocked: land unit 01001262012 (Čuibes iela 17) abuts land unit 01001262083 of the existing Delska LV DC4 record (curated:delska-lv-dc4-riga-latgales-463), so LV DC1/DC2 belong to the same campus, and that site's locator is a project_locator point that a new project cannot reuse, while a separate site would duplicate the campus.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated in-window Delska or government record stating LV DC1 (or LV DC2) operation, such as a Tier III Facility certification announcement or a BIS acceptance of a further stage, plus a geometry review giving the Čuibes iela 17 / Latgales iela 463 campus a reusable campus locator; then add the operating facility as a project on the existing Delska site.

entries.candidate: Bulk N01 Vennesla: planning for new buildings and plot preparation to increase capacity further (Bulk Q3 2026 report)

That would be a new project on the existing N01 site, but it is not expressible: the N01 site row lists two geometry evidence IDs against its one project, so the builder's locator inheritance fails, and the project's derivation code (source_attribute_decimal_coordinates_to_point_without_centroiding) is not one a new Point locator can state, so the campus point cannot be restated either. The future buildings are also unnamed.
